review_basis: All 80 actual cat images were visually reviewed. Descriptions prioritize visible coat, face, eyes, ears, paws and tail over breed-name assumptions. Anatomical right/left is specified for odd-colored eyes; other directional markings refer to the frontal input image and remain attached to the same body regions during motion.

templates.subject_definition: <Subject 1> is the individual cat in <Picture 1>. {description} Its appearance comes exclusively from this image; <Video 1> supplies the movement and interaction timing.
templates.retention: <Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - Preserve {anchor}. Keep its face, natural anatomy and individual marking placement consistent through turns, fast motion, partial occlusion and settling. Transfer the reference movement onto this same individual.
templates.opening: [Shot 1] <Subject 1> begins seated in <Subject 2>, matching <Picture 1>'s viewpoint and initial placement. Clearly show {anchor}. Keep these features attached to the same anatomical regions as the pose changes; the studio illumination and floor remain consistent.
templates.closing: Through the final frame, <Subject 1> retains {anchor}. Hold the specified ending pose with natural breathing, preserving this individual's face, proportions and markings.
